title: The 1,000-a-month Claude cap is used up at about 200 to 1,000 weekly users, so it bites at the first size, and lifting it costs cents
evidence: Claude asks per weekly user per month: upper 5.2 = (12.4 scans + 7.3 typed) x 26.6% (REPORT.md: 44% any answer minus 17.4% shop price; 109 scans, 64 typed, 19 devices, 14 days); central 2.5 and low 1.0 with assumed consent and cache rates. Cap 1,000 / 5.2 = 192 users, / 2.5 = 400, / 1.0 = 1,000 (catalogue-first.ts:150). Lifting it: 50,000 users x 2.5 to 5.2 asks x US$0.0007 to 0.00225 = US$88 to 585 a month on Haiku 4.5, US$11 to 76 on Haiku 5.5. Real ask rate never seen: all 191 probe answers have rangeAskedAt empty because probes carry no consent (work/answers.jsonl), and 93 of 191 ended with no basis, the case that would call Claude. Full table: cost-table.md
fix: Decide a ceiling in advance (for example 20,000 a month, worst case about US$46 at Haiku 4.5) and read the Mac range-ask count after the first week of real traffic to replace the assumed rates
fix_cost: 10 minutes plus a Mac read; under US$50 a month at the ceiling
dup_of: R33: adds the user count where it bites (192 to 1,000), the cost of lifting it at 10,000 and 50,000 users, and that the real ask rate is unmeasured

title: Claude Haiku 5.5 is listed at one tenth of the price of the Haiku 4.5 Pexi hard-codes, and Haiku 4.5 is still Active past its earliest retirement date
evidence: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing: "Claude Haiku 5.5 (for prompts up to 100,000 tokens) | $0.10 / MTok ... $0.50 / MTok" against "Claude Haiku 4.5 | $1 / MTok ... $5 / MTok". https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations: "claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 | Active | N/A | Not sooner than October 15, 2026" (date passed, no deprecation notice) and "claude-haiku-5-5 | Active | N/A | Not sooner than October 7, 2027". Code: RANGE_ASK_MODEL = claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (identify/src/range-ask.ts:213). Newer tokenizer gives about 30% more tokens (pricing page), already counted in cost-table.md
fix: Point RANGE_ASK_MODEL at claude-haiku-5-5 after one structured-output run with the same schema and a check that the answers stay sensible; keep the old id as a fallback
fix_cost: 1 hour; saves about 88% of the Claude bill and removes the retirement date risk until October 2027
dup_of: R34: adds that a 10x cheaper active replacement exists and that the Oct 15 2026 date has passed without notice (checked today)

title: The server spaces Open Food Facts lookups at about 100 a minute but Open Food Facts publishes 15 a minute per address, with an address ban as the penalty
evidence: Code: OFF_MIN_GAP_MS = 600 and the comment "publishes a read limit of 100 product requests a minute" (app/src/open-food-facts.ts:44-58). Page fetched with curl today, https://openfoodfacts.github.io/openfoodfacts-server/api/: "15 req/min/IP address for all read product queries" and "If these limits are reached, we reserve the right to deny you access to the website and the API through IP address ban." Every server lookup leaves from the one Mac address. At 50,000 weekly users the evening peak reaches about 17 a minute (0.41 scans per user per day x 50% reaching Open Food Facts x 10% in the peak hour, all assumed); under 10,000 it does not
fix: Change OFF_MIN_GAP_MS to 4,000 (15 a minute; R35 proposed about 12), keep the 429 pause, and correct the comment; or lean on the local catalogue and the downloadable data for the long tail
dup_of: R35: adds the published figure (15 a minute) against the code constant (100 a minute); the User-Agent half of R35 is already fixed in code

title: Overpass states 10,000 queries a day but "divide by 100" for regular use and "commercial use should use self-hosted or paid" servers; the store cache holds only 500 squares
evidence: https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Overpass_API: "No more than 10,000 queries per day", "If you set something up that uses the Overpass API regularly, then divide those numbers by 100", "Commercial use should use self-hosted or paid Overpass servers". Code: public server, 24 h cache per 1 km square, FIFO ceiling 500 squares (app/src/stores.ts:302, 338-340). Estimated queries a day: about 75 at 1,000 users, 750 at 10,000, 3,750 at 50,000 (25% daily active, 50% share location, 60% in a new square; all assumed), so the 100 a day guidance is passed near 1,300 users and the 500-square cache thrashes at 50,000
fix: Before launch growth, point SHIN_OVERPASS at a paid or self-hosted Overpass server, or cache squares for a week; price of a paid server not found
dup_of: R77: adds the published numbers (10,000 a day, divide by 100 for regular use, 500-square cache) and the user count where it bites; the User-Agent part of R77 not rechecked

title: RevenueCat is free below US$2.5K monthly tracked revenue, then 1% of all of it, and wants a card on file before that point
evidence: https://www.revenuecat.com/pricing/ (curl, text): "Once you reach $2.5K MTR, you'll be charged 1%. For $2.5K, we'll charge you $25. No charges apply on months when you don't hit the $2.5K threshold" and "if you don't provide credit card details and you reach $2.5k in MTR ... parts of the product will become unavailable until you do". Pexi reaches it only at 50,000 users with a 2% paying share (US$2,785 gross; fee US$27.85), or about 900 monthly subscribers at CA$3.99
fix: Put a card on the RevenueCat account before the first month over US$2.5K
fix_cost: 5 minutes; US$25 to 70 a month at 50,000 users

title: Apple 15% versus 30% is worth more money than any service Pexi pays for, and enrolment in the Small Business Program is still unrecorded
evidence: https://developer.apple.com/app-store/subscriptions/: "you receive 70% of the subscription price at each billing cycle" in the first year, "85%" after one year, and 85% from the start "if you're currently enrolled in the App Store Small Business Program". At CA$3.99 and a 2% share the gap is US$8 a month at 1,000 users, US$84 at 10,000, US$418 at 50,000 (5% share: US$21, US$209, US$1,044). money.jsonl round 1: enrolment not visible, App Store Connect not signed in
fix: Enrol in the Small Business Program in App Store Connect before the first sale and record the start date in RevenueCat
dup_of: blind 12 and money round 1 (Small Business Program unrecorded): adds the dollar size of the gap at each user count

title: One pack rebuild sends 340 GB through the home upload at 50,000 users (3.2 hours at the measured 234 Mbps), and a Cloudflare cache rule would remove it for free
evidence: Round 1 blind: pack 44,143,820 bytes uncompressed, about 6.8 MB compressed, "cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC", re-sent to every phone on a version change (app/public/js/pack.js:259-294). Arithmetic: 50,000 x 6.8 MB = 340 GB; 340e9 x 8 / 234e6 = 11,600 s = 3.2 hours; 10,000 users 0.6 hours. A scan answer is 1,389 bytes on average (work/answers.jsonl), so the pack is over 99.9% of all bytes. Cloudflare Free also restricts serving "a disproportionate percentage of pictures, audio files, or other large files" through the CDN without paid services (https://www.cloudflare.com/service-specific-terms-application-services/); whether a proxied binary API response counts is not stated
fix: Cache rule on /api/pack* (the URL is versioned and immutable) or host the pack on object storage; round 1 already proposed this
dup_of: blind round 1 item 8: adds 340 GB and 3.2 hours at 50,000 users, the 99.9% byte share, and the Cloudflare large-file clause

title: Cloudflare Free is labelled for hobby projects with no uptime guarantee, and its one rate-limit rule counts by address only
evidence: https://www.cloudflare.com/plans/: Free "$0 /month ... For personal or hobby projects that aren't business-critical"; Pro "$20 /mo billed annually, or $25/mo billed monthly"; Uptime SLA row "Free - Pro - Business 100%". https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/rate-limiting-rules/ Free column: "Number of rules | 1", "Counting periods | 10 s", "Counting characteristics | IP". So an address-keyed flood rule at the edge cannot be the fix for the IPv6 gap in abuse round 1; Pro would cost US$20 a month, about 4% of net revenue at 10,000 users and a 2% share
fix: Stay on Free until paying subscribers cover Pro; do the IPv6 /64 grouping in the server instead
dup_of: abuse round 1 item 2 (IPv6 limits): adds that the free edge rule cannot group by network

title: Running cost per user is small: variable cost is 3.7% of net revenue per paying-share user at the central ask rate, 25% at the worst, and fixed cost is about US$10 a month
evidence: Net revenue per weekly user per month at 2% share, 15% Apple: 0.02 x US$2.785 x 0.85 = US$0.047; Claude per user: central 2.5 x US$0.0007 = US$0.00175 (3.7%), upper 5.2 x US$0.00225 = US$0.0117 (25%); at 5% share the worst case is 10%. Fixed: Apple US$99 a year = US$8.25, domain about US$1.25 (assumed), Cloudflare US$0. About 4 subscribers at CA$3.99 pay the fixed costs. At 1,000 users net revenue is only US$39 to 118 a month (CA$54 to 165), which is the thin part, not the bill
dup_of: launch-gaps-2026-11-06 line 392 and decisions.md 2026-11-05 (per-scan cost estimate): agrees with it, adds 1,000/10,000/50,000-user totals against revenue

title: Hammer, Open Prices, Icecat, USDA, Statistics Canada and the BC liquor list cost nothing per user because they are offline imports, not runtime calls
evidence: grep over app/server.ts, app/src, app/public/js, mac for fetch and the vendor hosts: only open-food-facts.ts (live product lookup), stores.ts (Overpass), scan-quota.ts (RevenueCat) and the Anthropic SDK in identify/src make runtime calls; Hammer is a weekly import (mac/hammer-refresh.sh), Open Prices a bulk pull (price/src/openprices.ts), USDA and Icecat appear only in attribution and catalogue code. USDA FDC limit "1,000 requests per hour per IP address" (http://fdc.nal.usda.gov/api-guide/) is not reachable from a phone

evidence: server.ts:1667-1690 (device 12 per 10 minutes and 40 a day, weekly allowance applies to asks, network 100 per 10 minutes and 250 a day), scan-quota.ts SHIN_FREE_SCANS_PER_WEEK=10 and Plus 100 (REGISTER line 44: on in production since 2026-11-17), server.ts:1771-1775 packReadRefusal returns refused unless the device is listed as a developer.
